7.1.intro: Ten minutes of setup stops the most expensive Meta problems. We'll do it one small step at a time.

steps.say: Go to business.facebook.com/settings. Click **Users > People**, then **Invite people**. Invite a second person you trust with **Full control** (Meta's name for admin).
steps.check: **People** shows two people with full control.
steps.careful: With only one admin, if that person is locked out, you lose the account.
steps.lost: Invite one trusted person as a second admin.

steps.say: In Business Settings, open **Security Centre**. Turn on **Two-factor authentication** for everyone.
steps.check: Two-factor is required for all admins.
steps.lost: Turn on two-factor in **Security Centre**.

steps.say: In **Security Centre**, click **Start verification**. Enter your legal business name, address, phone and website.
steps.check: It shows "In review" or "Verified". No button, or "Ineligible"? Skip and come back later.
steps.lost: No verify button? That's okay. Skip this card.

steps.say:
Add the Facebook & Instagram sales channel in Shopify.

1. Click **Settings**, then **Sales channels**.
2. In the Shopify App Store, search **Facebook & Instagram** and add it.
3. Click **Start set up**, then **Connect account**.
4. Log in with Facebook, connect your things, click **Finish setup**.
steps.check: It shows under **Sales channels**, with your business, ad account, Page and pixel connected.
steps.lost: Add the **Facebook & Instagram** sales channel in Shopify.

steps.say: Go to **Sales channels > Facebook & Instagram > Settings > Data sharing settings**. Check customer data sharing is on. Choose **Maximum**. This helps fewer sales go missing.
steps.check: Data sharing says "Maximum".
steps.lost: Set data sharing to **Maximum**.

steps.say: Open **Events Manager**. Click your pixel. Look at the **Purchase** row in **Overview**.
steps.check: Purchase shows events from **Browser** and **Server**. Nothing yet? Place a small test order and check in an hour.
steps.lost: Look for **Purchase** in Events Manager. See it? Great.

steps.say:
Set a spending limit.

1. In Ads Manager, click the three-line menu.
2. Click **Billing and payments**, then **Payment settings**.
3. Find **Account spending limit**, click **Options**, then **Set limit**.
4. Type the most you're happy to spend in total. Save.
steps.check: The account stops at your limit, even if something goes wrong. It covers all-time spend and doesn't reset monthly.
steps.lost: Set an **Account spending limit**. Pick a number you're comfy with.

steps.say:
Make a "Daily" view.

1. Click **Columns**, then **Customise columns**.
2. Tick: Results, Cost per result, Amount spent, Purchase ROAS, CTR (link), Frequency.
3. Tick **Save as preset**, name it "Daily".
4. Click **Apply**.
steps.check: **Columns > Daily** shows your daily numbers.
steps.lost: Tick the six columns. Save as "Daily".

steps.say: Add a weekly 5-minute reminder: look for campaigns you didn't make, or budgets that jumped.
steps.check: The check is in your calendar. Find something odd? Turn it off, remove unknown people, contact Meta support, and tell your bank.
steps.lost: Add a weekly calendar reminder.

steps.say: Later, with a few hundred visitors: **All tools > Audiences > Create audience > Custom audience > Website**. Make "All visitors, last 30 days". Then 180 days, and buyers.
steps.check: They show "Ready" (can take a few hours).
steps.lost: Not enough visitors yet? Skip this for now.

7.2.intro: New sales campaigns start with Advantage+ on (automatic). Narrow the settings and it turns manual. Start automatic.

steps.say: In Ads Manager, click **+ Create**. Choose **Sales**, click **Continue**, then **OK**. Check **Advantage+** at the top right says **On**.
steps.check: Your main campaign for new customers is Advantage+.
steps.lost: **Create**, **Sales**, keep Advantage+ on.

steps.say: Only for warm audiences or a controlled test: **+ Create > Sales > Continue**, then set the audience or placements you need. Meta shows **Advantage+ off**.
steps.check: Warm and test campaigns are manual.
steps.lost: No warm campaign yet? Skip this card.

steps.say: In the ad, go to **Ad creative** and open **Enhancements** (Advantage+ creative). Turn off changes that alter how your ad looks. Check **Advanced preview** too.
steps.check: The preview shows your ad as you made it.
steps.lost: Turn off auto changes you don't like.

7.3.intro: The format is the shape of the ad. The right shape helps your message show.

steps.say: For each ad, pick a format from the lesson table. For most stranger ads: a single video.
steps.check: Every brief names one format.
steps.lost: Not sure? Use a single video.

steps.say: Make each ad in 4:5 (feed) and 9:16 (Stories and Reels).
steps.check: Each ad fits everywhere without cropping.
steps.lost: Make two sizes of each ad.

steps.say: Keep text inside the safe zones so buttons don't cover it.
steps.check: The preview shows no hidden text.
steps.lost: Keep text away from edges.

7.4.intro: Build ads in a switched-off campaign, copy them over, and turn them on together. That keeps tests fair.

steps.say: Open your switched-off build campaign. Click **Ads**. Click **+ Create** and make each new ad.
steps.check: New ads sit there with "Off" under **Delivery**.
steps.lost: Make the ad in your paused campaign.

steps.say: Tick the new ads. Click **Duplicate**. Choose your live campaign and ad set. Click **Duplicate** again.
steps.check: Copies appear in the live ad set, still off.
steps.lost: Tick, **Duplicate**, pick the live ad set.

steps.say: Open each copy. In **Ad setup**, choose **Use existing post**. Pick the original's post.
steps.check: Each copy shows the same post. Option missing? Publish the original first.
steps.lost: Choose **Use existing post** on each copy.

steps.say: Tick all the new copies. Turn them on together. Click **Publish** if asked.
steps.check: They all start on the same day.
steps.lost: Turn them all on at once.

steps.say: Leave them alone for 2 to 5 days before judging.
steps.check: You judge settled numbers.
steps.careful: Only schedule ads for a clear reason, like a sale start time.
steps.lost: Don't touch for a few days. That's the task.

7.5.intro: After you start or change an ad set, Meta needs days to learn. Some edits restart that.

steps.say: Before editing a live ad set, check if it restarts learning: adding or changing ads, changing the audience, event or bid strategy, pausing 7+ days, or a big budget change (a common guide is over 20%).
steps.check: You only make big edits on purpose.
steps.lost: Big change? Pause and think first.

steps.say: Start new tests as new campaigns instead of editing working ones.
steps.check: Working campaigns keep what they learned.
steps.lost: New test = new campaign.

steps.say: Judge on the last 7 days, not one day.
steps.check: A weaker second week doesn't panic you.
steps.careful: Copy winning ads instead of moving them, so each campaign keeps its learning.
steps.lost: Look at 7 days, not today.

7.6.intro: Ten minutes a day, same steps each time. **Your ads** in Helix shows the verdicts too.

steps.say: Pick today's word: push, careful push, hold or defend (Lesson 1.6).
steps.check: You have one word.
steps.lost: Not sure? Pick **hold**.

steps.say: In Ads Manager, set **Last 7 days**, choose **Columns > Daily**. On **Campaigns**, read **Amount spent** and **Frequency**.
steps.check: You know if any campaign overspends or tires people.
steps.lost: Look at spend and frequency. Anything strange?

steps.say: Grade each ad: **Star** (give more), **Steady** (leave), **Passenger** (leave), **Drain** (lots of spend, poor results: turn off).
steps.check: Drains are switched off.
steps.lost: Find one drain. Turn it off.

steps.say: Label each campaign: winning, learning, shaky or dying.
steps.check: Every campaign has a label.
steps.lost: One word per campaign.

steps.say: Take one action. Write it in your notes.
steps.check: One action, about 10 minutes total.
steps.lost: Do one thing. Write it down.

7.7.intro: Reach is how many people an ad can reach. An ad with tiny reach can't grow.

steps.say: On the **Ads** tab, set **Last 7 days**. Add **Reach** and **Frequency** columns. Click the **Reach** header to sort.
steps.check: You see which ads reach many people.
steps.lost: Sort your ads by **Reach**.

steps.say: Mark ads with big reach and an okay cost per sale. They can grow.
steps.check: You have a short list of ads that can take more spend.
steps.lost: Circle big-reach ads with okay costs.

steps.say: To spend more, pair a cheap low-reach ad with a big-reach ad in the same campaign.
steps.check: The campaign can grow without tiring people fast.
steps.lost: Put a big-reach ad next to your cheap one.

7.8.intro: Ads to strangers always look expensive, because Meta misses sales they cause later. Judge them fairly.

steps.say: Only compare stranger campaigns with other stranger campaigns.
steps.check: They're ranked against each other.
steps.lost: Strangers vs strangers only.

steps.say: Each week, check how many orders come from new customers.
steps.check: You know if stranger ads still bring new buyers.
steps.lost: Count new-customer orders this week.

steps.say: Judge stranger spend by your total MER trend on the Dashboard.
steps.check: You see the whole-store effect.
steps.careful: Only cut stranger spend when MER gets worse and new-customer orders drop.
steps.lost: Look at total MER, not just Meta.

7.9.intro: Some audiences don't know you, some do. Each has its own numbers to watch.

steps.say: Label each campaign Cold, Mixed, Warm or Hot in its name (Lesson 6.7).
steps.check: Every name shows its layer.
steps.lost: Add Cold or Warm to each name.

steps.say: Compare each campaign with the numbers for its layer in the lesson table.
steps.check: Each is judged against the right yardstick.
steps.lost: Compare cold with the cold row only.

7.10.intro: A scaling challenge is a planned 2 to 4 week push to spend more. Even if it fails, you learn.

steps.say: Make 6 to 10 new ads before you start.
steps.check: Fresh ads are ready.
steps.lost: Have new ads ready first.

steps.say: Write down the most you're willing to lose.
steps.check: You have a limit that ends the challenge.
steps.lost: Write one dollar limit.

steps.say: Open the campaign (campaign budget) or ad set (ad set budgets), raise **Daily budget** by 10% to 20%, click **Publish**. Write today's spend and reach.
steps.check: You can see if new spend finds new people.
steps.lost: Raise budget a little. Write it down.

steps.say: Stay at each new level for 10 to 14 days.
steps.check: MER has time to settle.
steps.lost: Wait about two weeks at each level.

steps.say:
Read the result.

- Spend grew much faster than reach? Add new ads, or remove some exclusions.
- MER didn't settle? Go back one step and find out why.
steps.check: You have a clear next action.
steps.lost: Didn't settle? Step back one level.

7.11.intro: Meta credits sales within 1 or 7 days of a link click, or 1 day of a view or other tap. That isn't the full truth, so we double-check.

steps.say: Click the **Columns** menu, then **Compare attribution models**. Tick **Incremental**, click **Apply**. It counts only sales Meta thinks the ad truly caused.
steps.check: You see how many sales are likely truly extra.
steps.lost: Optional. Skip if you don't see it.

steps.say: Each week, compare Meta's sales with your real Shopify sales and your MER.
steps.check: You trust your store's numbers first.
steps.lost: Shopify is the truth. Meta is a hint.

steps.say: When spend is big enough, run a holdout test (Lesson 20.9).
steps.check: You know how many sales ads really cause.
steps.lost: Small spend? Skip for now.

7.12.intro: Meta has a few common problems. Each one has a known fix.

steps.say: Find your problem in the lesson table.
steps.check: You have the matching fix.
steps.lost: Find your problem's row.

steps.say: Do the fix. Write it in your notes with the date.
steps.check: It's fixed, and you'll know what you did if it comes back.
steps.lost: Do the fix. Note the date.

7.13.intro: Your first ad needs only about eight settings. One campaign, 3 to 5 ads, a budget you're okay with. Or Helix can build it for you, switched off.

steps.say: In Events Manager, check your pixel shows **Purchase** events. No? Do Lesson 7.1 steps 4 to 6 first.
steps.check: You see Purchase events.
steps.lost: See **Purchase** in Events Manager? Then carry on.

steps.say:
Pick a daily budget.

- Selling under about $5,000 a month? $20 to $50 a day for two weeks.
- Selling more? About 2 times your break-even cost per sale (on **Profit**), inside your guide from Lesson 1.9.
steps.check: You have one daily budget, like $30.
steps.lost: Just starting? Pick $20 a day.

steps.say: Get 3 to 5 ads ready: short videos or pictures of your best seller, each with a different first line, in 4:5 and 9:16.
steps.check: 3 to 5 files, plus one main text and one headline.
steps.lost: Three pictures of your best seller. That's enough.

steps.say: Want Helix to build it? Click **Do it for me**, then skip to step 9. It's made switched off. Nothing spends until you turn it on.
steps.check: A paused campaign appears in Ads Manager.
steps.lost: Click **Do it for me**. Helix sets it up, switched off.

steps.say: Building it yourself? Click **+ Create**, choose **Sales**, **Continue**, **OK**, check Advantage+ says **On**, name it "01-Sales-First", click **Next**.
steps.check: The campaign page is open with Sales as the goal.
steps.lost: **Create**, **Sales**, **Next**.

steps.say: Type your daily budget. Under **Conversion**, check your pixel (or dataset) is picked and the event is **Purchase**.
steps.check: Budget and Purchase are set. If you see **Conversion location**, pick **Website**.
steps.lost: Budget in, **Purchase** picked.

steps.say: Leave the audience on Meta's suggestion and placements on **Advantage+ placements**. Click **Next**.
steps.check: You're on the ad screen. Country box? Pick where you ship.
steps.lost: Leave the defaults. Click **Next**.

steps.say:
Add your ads.

1. Click **Add media**, upload your files.
2. Paste text into **Primary text**.
3. Paste your headline.
4. Paste your product link in **Website URL**.
5. Check the phone preview.
steps.check: Every ad shows the right picture, text and link.
steps.lost: Upload, paste text, paste link. Check the preview.

steps.say: Go live. Built it yourself? Click **Publish**. Helix built it? Open it, check budget, ads and link, then turn its switch blue.
steps.check: **Delivery** shows "In review", then "Learning".
steps.lost: Check the link. Turn it on.

steps.say: Leave it for 3 days. Then compare cost per purchase with your break-even cost per purchase.
steps.check: You know which ads are under, near or over break-even.
steps.careful: Big edits in the first days restart learning. Only change something broken, like a wrong link.
steps.lost: Wait 3 days. Then compare one number.

7.14.intro: Ads Manager looks busy, but you only use a few parts. Let's find them.

steps.say: Open Ads Manager (adsmanager.facebook.com). Check the account name top left.
steps.check: You're in your store's ad account.
steps.lost: Open Ads Manager. Check the name.

steps.say: Set the date at the top right to **Last 7 days**.
steps.check: The table shows the last week.
steps.lost: Pick **Last 7 days**.

steps.say: Click **Columns**, choose **Daily** (or **Performance**).
steps.check: You see Results, Cost per result, Amount spent and ROAS.
steps.lost: Pick **Columns > Daily**.

steps.say: Click **Campaigns**, then a campaign name. Look at the three levels (campaign, ad set, ad) without changing anything. Close it.
steps.check: You know where budget, audience and ads live.
steps.careful: Your screen may look a bit different. Look for the same words: Create, Columns, Delivery, Results.
steps.lost: Just look. Don't change. Close it.

7.15.intro: Caps tell Meta the most you will pay. Try them only when a campaign is steady.

steps.say: Only try this when a campaign already has at least 50 sales a week and steady results. Meta suggests 50 to 100 or more a week. Check on the **Campaigns** tab.
steps.check: You know if the campaign is ready. If not, keep the default setting.
steps.lost: Wait until you get 50 sales a week.

steps.say: Find your break-even cost per sale from Lesson 1.5. Write it down.
steps.check: One number, for example $40.
steps.lost: Find your break-even cost per sale.

steps.say: Duplicate the campaign. In the copy, find **Bid strategy** (campaign if it uses campaign budget, else ad set). Choose **Cost per result goal** (once called a cost cap). Type a number a little under break-even, for example $36.
steps.check: A test copy that aims to keep the average cost per sale near your number. Not guaranteed.
steps.lost: Copy the campaign and type a number just under break-even.

steps.say: Set the budget a bit higher than normal. Caps often spend less than the budget, so a bigger budget gives Meta room.
steps.check: The capped copy is not starved of money.
steps.lost: Give the copy a bit more budget.

steps.say: Run both for 7 days. Compare total sales and cost per sale.
steps.check: You know if the cap made you more profit. If it barely spent, raise the cap by 10% and try again.
steps.lost: Wait 7 days and compare.

steps.say: Optional: in **Advertising settings** (**All tools**), look for **Value rules**. Not every account has them. They tell Meta to bid more for groups worth more to you, like an age group with bigger orders. Add one rule only if your own sales data proves that group spends more.
steps.check: At most one rule, backed by your own numbers.
steps.lost: Skip this unless your data proves it.
